body:
Audit every agent-facing string in `solace-cli/src` that names Gleam or `gleam.toml` and decide whether it applies to Rust. The observed run was told "this project has no Gleam code" and "no Gleam code of its own", and `GLEAM`/`reference.txt` still read as if Gleam is the only store.

1. Where both languages share a command or tier, say "Gleam or Rust" or "symbol-held source"; where only Gleam applies, say "Gleam only" and name the deferred Rust command (D-158 point 6).
2. Cover at least: `GLEAM`'s doc and gate, `lockdown::plain`, `plain_session`, `grep`/`read`/`view` hints, `agent_reference`, `reference.txt`'s Files by tier and Rust projects sections, and `submit`/`delete`/`check`/`test` refusals.
3. Do not change behavior; this is wording only. Keep `gleam.toml` where the file is genuinely Gleam's; use `Cargo.toml` where Rust's.
4. Tests: assert a Rust project's refusal does not say "no Gleam code"; assert an unsupported Rust command says "Gleam only" rather than "no Gleam code"; assert the reference names both languages. Run `rust-unit` and `rust-acceptance`.

Left out: adding Rust `extract`, `merge`, `probe` or `format`; a language-neutral spelling for `gleam.toml` (it is a Gleam file).
title: commands: say Rust where they say Gleam
